title: Response lifecycle cohort profiling diary
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is a scratch diary for a small, pragmatic profiling run aimed at answering: which request cohorts (by prompt length, coldstart vs warm, and model variant) are driving p99 end-to-end latency and which internal stages dominate. Not a polished report — notes + numbers + quick microbenchmarks and suggested follow-ups.

Sampling methodology (how I pulled traces):
- Time window: 72h (2025-10-28T00:00 -> 2025-10-31T00:00) across prod-region-us-west1.
- Total traces sampled: 10,384 end-to-end traces (random sample with stratification).
- Stratification keys: user-visible sequence length bins (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024), coldstart flag (container coldstart within last 60s), and model_variant (redwood-v1-7b, open-llama-13b).
- Only successful responses included (status 200); error traces analyzed separately.
- For each trace we extracted stage timestamps: ingress_receive, routing/selection, queue_enter, batch_wait_start, batch_dispatch, kernel_start, kernel_end, kv_cache_lookup_start, kv_cache_lookup_end, egress_serialize, egress_send.

Top-line aggregated quantiles (all cohorts combined):
- p50 E2E: 62 ms
- p95 E2E: 154 ms
- p99 E2E: 488 ms

Per-stage median and tail (coarse):
- ingress_receive: p50=1ms, p95=3ms, p99=12ms
- routing/selection: p50=2ms, p95=8ms, p99=25ms
- queue_wait (time between queue_enter and batch_start): p50=6ms, p95=48ms, p99=220ms
- batch_dispatch overhead (serialization + enqueue): p50=4ms, p95=12ms, p99=30ms
- kernel_exec (kernel_start -> kernel_end): p50=40ms, p95=70ms, p99=190ms
- kv_cache_lookup (for requests with cache key attempts): p50=1ms, p95=6ms, p99=55ms
- egress_serialize + send: p50=3ms, p95=7ms, p99=20ms

Key cohort findings (high-level):
1) Long-sequence requests (257-1024 tokens) account for ~7% of requests but ~48% of p99 mass. Their kernel_exec p99 is ~780ms in isolation (when seqlen >> kv reads) — unsurprising but worth accounting in routing policy.
2) Coldstart traces are a small fraction (~3%) but disproportionately appear at p99: coldstart p99 E2E = 1.2s vs warm p99 = 420ms. Root cause in most coldstart hits: additional kv_cache_miss penalty and sometimes an extra 60–120ms container init tail depending on node warming.
3) Mid-length responses (65-256 tokens) show the most variability in queue_wait: p95 queue_wait jumps from ~40ms normally to 220ms during microbursts (see next).
4) Microburst behavior: windows of 30–90s where queue_wait p99 spikes — correlates with upstream client-side batching (see trace cohort examples 2025-10-29T14:02Z trace ids in linked set).
5) KV cache misses matter at tail: for requests that attempt KV lookups, p99 lookup time has a bimodal distribution — most are <10ms, but ~0.6% show 40–120ms due to behind-the-scenes async fetch fallbacks. These coincide with cold container lanes and egress network retries.

Illustrative cohort breakdown (numbers approximate from sample):
- Short (0-64): 68% of requests — p50=48ms, p95=120ms, p99=300ms. Main contributor to tail: queuing + occasional KV miss.
- Mid (65-256): 25% — p50=86ms, p95=210ms, p99=560ms. Strong sensitivity to batching cadence.
- Long (257-1024): 7% — p50=320ms, p95=600ms, p99=1200ms. Kernel_exec dominates.

Microbenchmarks we ran (quick notes):
- Single-request kernel-only runs on an identical GPU instance (no batching): for redwood-v1-7b, seqlen 512 kernel-only p50=180ms, p95=250ms, p99=420ms. These align with kernel_exec portion extracted from live traces (sanity check).
- KV cache synthetic workload: 10k lookups against local cache host (same network fabric) shows p99=8ms; when introducing a simulated cold container (evicted local cache), remote fallback p99 jumps to 85ms. Conclusion: remote fallback path and its retry/backoff amplify kv lookup tail.
- Async-batching experiment (alpha branch): turning on async batch drain with max-wait 6ms reduced overall p95 by ~12% for mid-length cohort but increased p50 by ~4ms. Tradeoff looks acceptable for mid/short cohorts.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
- Routing: add a policy to route seqlen >= 512 to a heavy-worker pool (or to a model variant with larger batch-capacity) to isolate long-kernel requests from short ones. Quick win.
- Coldstart mitigation: aggressive prewarmed min-instance policy for dedicated pools that serve critical SLAs; for hosted lanes, prioritize coldstart reduction by reducing cold-container penalty path (investigate the 60–120ms init step observed on specific node images).
- KV cache: instrument and add telemetry for fallback counts and latencies (already filed INF-512). Add a circuit-breaker / fast-path that returns a cached-empty token quickly while triggering a background refresh to avoid tail amplification.
- Batching policy: enable async draining for mid/short cohorts in an A/B bucket (10% traffic) and measure downstream p95 and token-cost tradeoff. We've got a PR (#847) with the alpha implementation.

Longer-term / strategic items:
- Work with model-onboarding to create per-variant kernel profile artifacts (p50/p95/p99 by seqlen) that can be used by router to make more informed decisions at request time.
- Investigate network stack differences on the nodes that show persistent KV lookup tails — seems correlated with a subset of SKU revisions in us-west1. Could be NIC firmware / kernel offload settings.
- Consider KV-cache local replication (hot-key replication) for top 1% of heavy keys identified from access logs.

Open questions / things to re-run before shipping any wider recommendations:
- Are the KV tail spikes reproducible in a controlled repro that mimics the exact container lifecycle and fallback code-paths? I have a partial repro but need to coordinate with infra to replicate node SKUs.
- How stable is the microburst pattern? Sampling over a longer window (2 weeks) to verify seasonality.
- Cost impact of async draining at fleet-scale — need to model tokens/sec vs effective latency improvements.

Notes-to-self / trace bookmarks:
- See sample traces: trace-20251029-140215 (mid-cohort microburst), trace-20251030-033012 (coldstart kv-fallback), trace-20251028-201100 (long-seq kernel tail). Saved in trace-store under /tmp/prof-sample-2025-11-02.tar.gz.
- Follow up with Diego on infra repro for KV fallback (Diego assigned INF-512).
- Priya to spin up A/B for async-batching alpha, target 10% traffic for 48h and report p50/p95/p99 by cohort.

Conclusion (raw):
- p99 is a multi-factor sum: long kernel execs + rare coldstart penalties + occasional kv fallback + queuing during microbursts. No single silver-bullet, but likely ~60% of p99 mass is mitigatable by (1) better routing for long-seq and (2) KV fallback optimization.
- Next week: run 2-week sampling, validate KV repro, and get async-batching A/B results.

(End of diary entry — will convert to a polished postmortem if any of the cohorts cause customer-impact tickets.)
